Photograph: Sarah Wilson/AAP Blue Mountains Police allege mother stabbed three children in Blue Mountains leaving one child dead Bystanders found all four on the side of the road at Valley Heights on Sunday with stabbing injuries Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Ima Caldwell and AAP Sun 20 Sep 2026 22.19 EDT First published on Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.43 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Police have alleged that a mother was behind a stabbing attack on three young children that left one dead and two others fighting for their lives in hospital. The woman, aged in her 40s, is also in a critical condition. Bystanders were first on the scene after finding the three children and the woman with stab wounds inside a vehicle at Valley Heights in the Blue Mountains , west of Sydney, on Sunday afternoon. One young child died at the scene despite witnesses rushing to help, delivering first aid while waiting for emergency services to arrive. The alleged domestic violence incident came at the end of a horror weekend across New South Wales , after three women were allegedly murdered inside their homes within a 12-hour period on Saturday. Three men charged with domestic violence-related murders after three women killed in separate incidents in NSW Read more The police deputy commissioner Peter McKenna described the past two days as devastating. “It’s a horrific and tragic weekend and it’s like one that I don’t remember in my career,” he told Nine’s Today on Monday. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email “Those three … plus the no-more-tragic situation that we had in the Blue Mountains. Put them all together and it’s unfathomable.” Paramedics treated the mother and children at the scene on Sunday before taking them by road to Westmead hospital and Westmead Children’s hospital in a critical condition. “The two children and their mother are in a critical condition,” McKenna said. “The mother is the suspect in this matter, for domestic related homicide, and that investigation is ongoing.” McKenna told reporters on Monday the woman remained in a critical condition and police had “to wait for the medical side to play out”. “If she recovers from those injuries, certainly our people … will be intent on charging [her] with homicide,” he said. Hours after the incident, NSW police Supt John Nelson said the father of the children had been notified. The father had been at work when he received the call from police, he said. “You can imagine receiving that tragic news,” Nelson told reporters. McKenna said the father was immediately taken to hospital. “He’s supporting these two children that are in a pretty good condition at the moment. He’s assisting us with the investigation,” he said. He said the woman had not previously come to the attention of police and that investigators were not looking for anyone else in relation to the incident. The woman was aged in her 40s and the children were all under five. All three had undergone surgery in hospital. Nelson praised the efforts of the “upstanding” members of the public who responded to the tragic scene. “People are just going about a lovely Sunday afternoon, and being confronted with this is traumatic and tragic for anybody,” he said. Responding officers would not be spared the hardship and would have access to available support services. Police said the weapon used and the circumstances surrounding the incident would form part of their investigation. Blue Mountains councillor Darren Rodrigo on Sunday described the news as “absolutely horrendous and tragic”. “Our deepest love and condolences to the immediate family and our prayers with all the children involved,” he said. “A massive thank you to the community members [who] intervened to provide medical assistance and to our first responders for their incredible support and courage during this time.” Separately, McKenna said the weekend had been “tragic and horrific … in relation to domestic violence”, referring to three other alleged homicides in NSW. “We’ve had four incidents, one at Wagga, one at Tenterfield, one at Bondi and … terrible scenes at the Blue Mountains yesterday,” he said. He said police would allege that in all four incidents “knives or edged weapons were used”. “It’s actually very, very confronting,” McKenna told reporters. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/.text: Scandal în Parlament pe șefia Curții de Conturi. Fostul parlamentar PSD de Buzău, Sorin Lazăr, a fost ales președinte interimar al instituției cu voturile PSD, AUR și UDMR. PNL și USR i-au acuzat pe social-democrați că fac, din nou, alianță cu AUR pentru a-și impune oamenii în funcții-cheie. Potrivit informațiilor Digi24, postul de președinte cu mandat deplin ar fi păstrat pentru actualul vicepremier PSD, Marian Neacșu, după plecarea sa din Guvern. Adrian Echert, deputat USR : „Cei de la PSD au nevoie de anumite voturi doar pentru învestirea Guvernului. Pentru că pentru orice altceva există AUR. E ca în reclama aia celebră”. Gabriela Horga, senatoare PNL: „Am văzut azi din nou cum alianța PSD-AUR merge înainte, cum alianța PSD-AUR a mai capturat încă o instituție a statului. Voi cei de la AUR care le spuneți oamenilor că sunteți în opoziție față de PSD, cum ați dat putere PSD să pună un președinte interimar la Curtea de Conturi, în loc să se demareze procedura de numire a noilor membri, așa cum prevede legea”. Social-democrații au ieșit cu un contraatac, iar cei de la AUR au negat alianța. Adrian Câciu, deputat PSD: „ P olul format din trompetele musca și țânțarul, cum le zic eu, sau pițigoii de la PNL și USR nu au alt obiectiv decât distrugerea poporului român”. Petrișor Peiu, senator AUR: „Îi incurajez pe colegii de la PNL și USR să deschidă orice manual de politologie și o să vadă că definiția majorității guvernamentale e simplă: parlamentarii care votează învestirea guvernului. Le mai aduc aminte că le-am promis că la prima moțiune de cenzură împotriva guvernului vom vota alături de dvs. Curaj!”. Funcția de președinte al Curții de Conturi a rămas vacantă în iulie 2025, după plecarea lui Mihai Busuioc la Curtea Constituțională. Interimatul a fost preluat atunci de Mirela Călugăreanu, fostă șefă a Fiscului. Potrivit informațiilor Digi24, mandatul deplin ar fi dorit de vicepremierul PSD Marian Neacșu, după ieșirea din Guvernul Luca Niculescu. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News
